name: browser_history
description: Query a browser history database from a copy of it and its -wal, -shm and -journal sidecars, made in a private directory (mode 0700, in TMPDIR, /tmp or /var/tmp) that is never $OUT and removed afterwards: the copy holds the evidence's secrets until the withholding below has run, so a run killed with SIGKILL leaves it outside the job's output (a stop signal removes it; after SIGKILL it stays in the temporary directory until the host clears it). Named queries: chrome_visits and firefox_visits (every visit joined to its URL: visit id, raw time and microsecond ISO time, transition or visit type with its raw value, referring visit), chrome_url_summary and firefox_url_summary (ONE ROW PER URL with a visit count and the last visit: a summary, not a visit list; chrome_history and firefox_history are their old names, answered with a note), chrome_downloads, firefox_downloads, tables; or your own SELECT, WITH or PRAGMA. Read-only twice: a statement must start with SELECT, WITH or PRAGMA, and the copy is opened with a SQLite authorizer that denies every action but reading and the pragmas that only report. It reports wal_present (a -wal was beside the database) and wal_frames_replayed (valid frames SQLite found in the copy of the log and checkpointed into the copy; 0 for a damaged or refused log), never merely that a sidecar was copied. Nothing in a WAL or a rollback journal names the database it was written for, so wal_inspection reads the log's own header, salts, checksums and committed frames and compares what the formats allow with the database (page size; text encoding and schema cookie from the last committed page 1); a log or journal that contradicts the database is not copied (wal_refused, journal_refused), the wal-index (-shm) is never copied, and wal_not_established says what cannot be told. The evidence may be read-only: the copies are made owner-only and writable. SENSITIVE: before any query, every trigger of the copy is dropped, then every cell of a credential column (logins.password_value, cookies.value and encrypted_value, moz_cookies.value, Firefox key4.db metadata and nssPrivate; any column whose name says password, secret, token, encrypted, card, cc, cvc, cvv, pin, ssn or iban, a number or real included; the text columns of a table named for cards or IBANs) and every text cell that is wholly a card number (13 to 19 digits passing the Luhn check) is replaced in the copy by a marker holding only its length, and the answer lists what was withheld and how many triggers were dropped. The secrets of every URL in a returned cell are found by parameter name and by user-info: the value of a query-string or fragment parameter whose name says token, secret, password, key, session, signature and the like (the list is in the tool) and the password of the user-info are replaced the same way and listed in url_secrets_withheld; a token under another parameter name, or in a path, is not found and is printed with the rest (measured on generated canaries: every one of the 20 printed whole in a path and under an unlisted name, 0 under a listed name or in user-info; the tests plant them again); write_url_secrets: true writes their whole text to a 0600 file under $OUT, in a job only. No flag brings a column value back, and nothing is decrypted. Usernames, URLs (secrets withheld) and dates are returned. A cell longer than 4096 (the bytes of a blob, the characters of a text) is shown inline by its type and length alone, and the whole row is in the file the page names; a blob that is not that long is returned as hex. A cell longer than 32 MiB is refused by SQLite (SQLITE_LIMIT_LENGTH), so a query that would build one (randomblob(100000000)) answers failed inside bounded memory. Two Luhn-valid card numbers of one length under one key (autofill's name and value) are both withheld, each marker carrying its row id. A file that is not a SQLite database is answered with sqlite_header: false and its size, never its bytes. The tool has its own clock (80 s of the manifest's 90): when it runs out the work stops, the pages written so far are placed and named, and the answer is partial with a status_basis that says where it stopped and how many statements and rows were read; every answer carries status and status_basis (complete only for an input read to its end), a wrong-type argument is refused as JSON (status failed), and SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP end it with one JSON document (status failed with interrupted true, exit 128 plus the signal) and no temporary file. A result file is never replaced: the same result keeps its name, another takes the next free -n name. The clock runs inside the copy of the database and its sidecars, the withholding UPDATEs and the caller's SQL (SQLite is asked every 1,000 steps whether the time is up); a clock that runs out before the withholding has finished means nothing was queried. The sidecars the tool refused to apply (wal_refused, journal_refused) make the status partial.

path.description: Path to History, places.sqlite or another SQLite database

query.description: chrome_visits | chrome_url_summary | chrome_downloads | firefox_visits | firefox_url_summary | firefox_downloads | tables (chrome_history and firefox_history still answer, as the URL summaries)

sql.description: Your own SELECT, WITH or PRAGMA, instead of a named query

limit.description: Rows shown inline per statement (default 200, 1 to 10000, an inline page size); every row is kept, and when there are more (or a cell was cut) the whole rows are written as JSON Lines and named in all_results

write_url_secrets.description: Write the whole text of every URL whose secrets were withheld, with the secret value, to a file under $OUT (mode 0600, created first, never replaced). Secret output: refused as JSON, before anything is created, unless the job runs with secret_output (the manifest declares it for this parameter); default false
